newsitem.title: USA: Anheuser sees '97 EPS growth below long-term goal.
newsitem.headline: Anheuser sees '97 EPS growth below long-term goal.

text.p: Anheuser-Busch Cos Inc said Wednesday it expects earnings per share growth in 1997 to be slighly below its long-term growth objective of double-digit gains, due to unexpectedly high levels of discounts in the beer industry.

"Our objective continues to be annual double-digit earnings per share growth," chairman August Busch III said in a news release. "However, given the current pricing environment, we now expect earnings per share growth for the full year to be consistent with year-to-date results, slightly below our long-term growth objective."
The company reported fully diluted earnings from continuing operations of $1.27 a share for the first six months of 1997, up from $1.23 a share a year ago.
Anheuser-Busch also said its share of beer shipments for the first six months of 1997 was 44.3 percent, essentially unchanged from the year-ago period.
Anheuser-Busch shares were down 1-3/8 at 46-1/2 Wednesday.
